title: Org capacity 1:1 scratch — hiring prioritization
content:
Quick purpose: prep notes for 1:1 with Daniela (people ops lead) — align on headcount plan for Q2-Q3, escalate role priorities, cover interview bandwidth and debrief follow-ups. This is messy — brain dump + talking points + live numbers for the meeting.

Snapshot (as of 2026-03-05):
- Open reqs: 18 (engineering 9, product 3, infra/ops 3, sales/growth 3)
- Offers extended (last 30d): 6, accepted: 4, declined: 2 (decline reasons: comp out of band x1, relocation/visa x1)
- Avg time-to-offer: 29 days (target 30)
- Interviewer pool: ~22 active interviewers (avg available hours/week: 6)
- Interviewer fatigue: several ICs flagged >6 panels/wk in last 3 weeks (infra, serving-runtime)
- Req priority tags (internal): P0 (3 roles), P1 (8), P2 (7)

Key constraints to call out:
- Hiring budget still constrained vs plan: CFO flagged 20% reduction in new hire budget for H2 unless enterprise revenue hits milestone X. Need headcount scenarios.
- Dedicated GPU hiring (serving-runtime) has ripple effect — if we freeze, delivery timeline for Dedicated product features slips 6–8 weeks.
- Interview rubric drift on backend SRE candidates — inconsistent scoring from new interviewers.

Questions for Daniela (high-priority):
1) Can we reallocate 4 budgeted hires from Q3 -> Q2 if we get early enterprise commit? What exact threshold triggers reallocation?
2) Is there appetite for short-term contractor hires for infra (6–12 weeks) to avoid backfill bottleneck? (pros/cons: faster, more costly, short ramp)
3) If we impose a temporary freeze on non-customer-facing roles, do we have a safe list of exemptions (critical infra, security)?
4) Any update on visa/relocation policy flexibility (remote-first exceptions) to improve accept rate?

Interview loop notes / pain points to raise:
- Panel composition: inexperienced interviewers (new managers) are inconsistent; propose mandatory calibration session (30m) before paneling for critical roles.
- Scheduling latency: average scheduling lag 6 days (candidate wait window increases withdraw risk). Consider hiring a 0.5 FTE coordinator for high-volume lanes.
- Score normalization: introduce numeric band and mandatory note for outlier scores (>=2 stdev from mean).
- Debrief follow-ups: ensure action owner and timeline are recorded on every debrief (we're missing closures).

Scenarios to propose (three-tier):
- Scenario A (green): Budget restored — hire all P0 + 75% P1 in Q2; add 2 contractor infra for quick wins. Outcome: maintains roadmap, minimal timeline slip.
- Scenario B (moderate): 20% budget cut — freeze P2, delay 50% P1 to Q3; hire 2 P0 only, plus 1 contractor for SRE. Outcome: product roadmap sees small backlog but critical path protected.
- Scenario C (restrictive): 40% cut — freeze all non-critical hires, only backfills for customer-SLA-impacting roles. Outcome: feature roadmap delays 2–3 months; need communications plan to customers and sales.

Immediate asks / decisions needed in meeting:
- Approve hiring prioritization (pick scenario or hybrid)
- Decision on contractor option (yes/no, hire ops team to scope)
- Approval to run 1 calibration session next week for infra/backend interviewers
- Temporary scheduler budget (0.5 FTE) — approve pilot for 8 weeks?

Draft meeting agenda (20–30m):
- 0–3m: Quick context & numbers (I present snapshot)
- 3–10m: Constraints and risk (budget, visa, interviewer capacity)
- 10–18m: Walk through scenarios A/B/C — get direction on prioritization
- 18–25m: Tactical asks (contractor, scheduler, calibration) and owners/dates
- 25–30m: Quick sync on comms to managers + next check-in cadence

Candidate pipeline mini-table (to reference):
- Eng: 9 open => 2 onsites scheduled this week, 3 in screening, 4 sourcing
- Product: 3 open => 1 offer pending, 2 sourcing
- Infra/Ops: 3 open => 1 strong onsite (lead), 2 need hiring manager feedback
- Sales/Growth: 3 open => 1 offer accepted, 1 offer pending, 1 sourcing

Debrief actions (ongoing issues I've logged):
- Infra debrief #INF-2026-02: Improve rubric for system design (owner: Riley) — due 2026-03-09 (missed) — push new due 2026-03-16.
- SRE panel ramp: add 2 senior interviewers as co-panellists (owner: Maya) — reach out by 2026-03-10 (incomplete).
- Candidate withdraw analysis: 2 recent declines — ask recruiting to capture reason code in ATS (owner: recruiting lead) — set by 2026-03-12.

Notes to self (things to not forget):
- Bring up cross-team hiring pipeline (console & serving-runtime both competing for same ICs) — ask if we can centralize shortlist and avoid double-interviews.
- Ask for clarity on internal mobility — can we convert backfill reqs to internal transfers faster?
- Prepare a 1-slide risk-to-roadmap visualization if they ask for impact quantification (I can whip it up in 15–20m).

Action items I will own after this meeting (provisional):
- Draft final prioritized req list (based on decision) and send to Recruiting by EOD 2026-03-13.
- Book a 30m calibration session (invite: interviewers for P0 infra + new managers) — target 2026-03-18.
- Scope contractor plan: 2 vendors, estimated ramp + cost, summary for Daniela — due 2026-03-19.

Open questions I still need to answer before meeting (quick research tasks):
- Exact FY budget delta thresholds for auto-freeze vs manual approval (finance runbook). Linked to CONF-people/team-headcount-2026.
- Current candidate offer comps vs market (recruiting to pull last 6mo offer comps by role).
- Confirm which hires are legally constrained (visa-heavy roles) so freeze policy can be nuanced.

Tone/ask guidance: be pragmatic, show 2–3 clear options (don’t leave Daniela with open-ended asks). Emphasize protecting customer-facing and security-critical roles first. Ask for explicit decision in the meeting or a firm timeline for follow-up.

End notes / quick timeline:
- Meeting scheduled: 2026-03-06 11:00 (30m) — adjust docs before meeting (I should update numbers live).
- Follow-up: Plan to send final decision + req list within 48 hours of meeting.

Random scratch ideas to test in meeting if time:
- Small hiring lottery: prioritize 2 hires this quarter in infra and 1 in product and run a cross-functional shadowing to accelerate onboarding.
- Swap: invite a senior PM to own part of onboarding plan to reduce time-to-productivity.
